The three companies below come from three different corners of the market (healthcare, net-lease real estate and integrated energy). Each one passes the same safety tests: a dividend covered by cash generation, a manageable balance sheet, and a payment record you can check line by line. The anchor of the group, Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ | JNJ Price Prediction), marked its 64th consecutive year of dividend increases with its latest raise. Pour a coffee and take your time with these. Johnson & Johnson makes money in two ways. Its Innovative Medicine segment sells prescription drugs for cancer, immune diseases and brain disorders, and its MedTech segment sells heart devices, surgical tools, contact lenses and orthopaedic implants. In the third quarter, worldwide sales reached $25.4 billion, with Innovative Medicine contributing $16.8 billion and MedTech $8.6 billion. Management says the company is on track to top $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time in its 140-year history. At a share price of $276.25, that works out to a yield of about 1.94%. The yield is modest partly because the stock has gained 51.06% over the past year. Safety read: Updated guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $11.05 to $11.15, so the forward dividend uses roughly 48% of the midpoint. Free cash flow is guided to $21 billion for the year, and the third quarter alone produced more than $6 billion. The company held about $17 billion in cash against roughly $45 billion of debt, a net debt position near $28 billion for a company worth about $665B. The chief financial officer listed the ability to "increase our annual dividend" among the company’s core capital priorities. Track record: The quarterly payout climbed from $1.19 in early 2024 to $1.24, then $1.30, and now $1.34, consistent with its Dividend King status. Bull case: The drug pipeline is carrying the company past the loss of STELARA exclusivity. Oncology grew about 17% in the quarter, TREMFYA rose 68.2%, and the company now has 29 products and platforms making at least $1 billion a year. Chief Executive Joaquin Duato told analysts, "We have a clear path to double-digit growth by the end of the decade." Risk: Talc litigation still hangs over the stock. The company agreed to a $5.5 billion ovarian talc resolution, but it requires participation from at least 95% of claimants. Related charges cut reported third-quarter EPS to $0.09, against adjusted EPS of $2.59. Questions to research: Will the talc settlement reach its participation threshold? And what does the December 8, 2026 Enterprise Business Review say about the 2027 outlook and the plan to fix MedTech? Realty Income (NYSE:O) is a landlord. It owns 15,536 properties rented to 1,842 clients across 96 industries, mostly on long-term net rented where tenants cover property-level expenses. The average remaining lease term is about 8.5 years, and occupancy is 98.8%. That combination of long contracts and full buildings is why the rent checks keep coming. Yield: At $59.05 a share, Realty Income offers a high-yield 5.20%. The current monthly payment is $0.2715, an annualized $3.258, and the next one coming November 13. Safety read: REITs are judged on adjusted funds from operations (AFFO), a cash-flow measure. Guidance calls for AFFO of $4.45 to $4.46 per share, so the annualized dividend uses about 73% of the low end. Chief Executive Sumit Roy said the "AFFO payout ratio, it’s amongst the lowest it has been in the history of Realty Income." The balance sheet carries a Fitch 'A' rating with a stable outlook, net debt of 5.4x EBITDA, and over 94% of its pro rata debt at fixed rates. Available liquidity stands at roughly $5.4 billion. Track record: The company has declared 676 consecutive monthly dividends. It announced its 116th consecutive quarterly dividend increase in September, its 136th increase since its 1994 NYSE listing. It is part of to the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index. The monthly payment has stepped up from $0.2695 a year ago to today’s $0.2715. Bull case: Re-leased properties are renting at 103.5% of prior rent, and third-quarter investments earned a 6.8% initial cash yield at a spread of about 170 basis points over the cost of capital. Management also lowered its credit loss expectation to about 30 basis points. Risk: Interest costs are climbing. Interest expense rose to $333.6M from $294.5M, and rising Treasury yields tend to weigh on REIT share prices. Questions to research: Data centers made up 11.7% of new property investment in the quarter, and Europe drew $940.1 million. Are you comfortable with that shift away from a U.S. retail landlord? And how much of future AFFO growth depends on acquisitions versus built-in rent increases? Chevron (NYSE:CVX) pumps oil and natural gas, refines it into fuels and chemicals, and sells those products worldwide. Upstream operations produced about 3.98 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter. U.S. refineries ran at a record 1.09 million barrels per day. Owning both the wells and the refineries helps smooth out cash flow when one side of the business weakens. Yield: At $212.73, the stock yields 3.07%. The quarterly dividend is $1.78, or $7.12 annualized, payable December 10 to holders of record on November 18. Safety read: Third-quarter adjusted EPS of $5.28 means the quarterly dividend took about 34% of that quarter’s adjusted earnings. Free cash flow reached $12.0B in the quarter. The balance sheet is conservative: debt-to-equity of 0.22, net debt of 0.94 times EBITDA, and interest coverage of 13.7x. Chevron cut debt by $3.5B and lowered net debt by $7.8B in the quarter. Track record: Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner called dividend growth the company’s first priority: "We’ve done that for 39 consecutive years. We’ll continue to do that." The payment history backs her up: the quarterly payout rose from $1.42 in 2022 to $1.51, $1.63, $1.71 and now $1.78. Bull case: Chevron hit its $3B structural cost reduction target six months early and is aiming for up to $4B by year end. The Hess integration delivered $1.5B in run-rate synergies, and U.S. production reached a record 2,077 MBOED. Lower costs raise the buffer under the dividend at any oil price. Risk: Oil prices drive the cash. Brent averaged $97/bbl in the quarter against $69 a year earlier, and management noted prices swung between $68 and $132 a barrel within the quarter. Today’s free cash flow shows high prices that may not last. Questions to research: Chevron releases a quarterly "Sensitivities and Forward Guidance" document. How much does earnings power shift with each move in Brent? And how much Venezuela exposure, where joint ventures plan to invest $7 billion over five years, fits your comfort level? Johnson & Johnson brings the longest raise run and a payout near half of adjusted earnings, while Realty Income delivers monthly income supported by an A-rated balance sheet and AFFO that covers its dividend. Chevron pairs a growing quarterly payout with the strongest free cash flow of the group. Each gets its cash from a different source, so together they give a retirement portfolio three dividend streams that hold up against one another’s weak spots. title: Will Suncor's Refining Strength Continue to Drive Cash Flow? - The Globe and Mail
content: Suncor Energy Inc. SU continues to benefit from its integrated refining operations, supported by stronger refining margins, high utilization and growing refined product sales. The company's downstream business has become a significant contributor to cash generation, raising expectations about its ability to sustain profitability. In the third quarter of 2026, Suncor's Refining and Marketing segment generated C$3.61 billion in adjusted funds from operations, compared with C$1.22 billion a year earlier. Segment free funds flow increased to C$3.29 billion from C$926 million, reflecting favorable refining conditions. Higher cracking margins were a major contributor to the improvement. Operational performance remained encouraging, with refinery utilization reaching 95% and crude throughput of approximately 488,000 barrels per day. Refined product sales increased to a third-quarter record of nearly 677,000 barrels per day from approximately 647,000 barrels a year earlier. Previous debottlenecking initiatives expanded high-value export capacity, while stronger domestic retail sales supported performance. Suncor's integrated operations provide another advantage. The Edmonton refinery's direct connection to oil sands production improves feedstock flexibility and operational efficiency. This integration helped maintain refinery throughput during planned maintenance, while logistics capabilities largely offset supply disruptions in Eastern Canada. Looking ahead, Suncor's 511,000-barrel-per-day refining network, diverse crude sourcing and access to high-value markets support its cash generation potential. However, sustaining the recent momentum will depend on refining margins, product demand and continued operational reliability. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM also benefited from favorable refining conditions in the third quarter of 2026. The company's Energy Products earnings increased to $7.17 billion from $1.84 billion a year earlier. ExxonMobil achieved 100% crude unit utilization at the U.S. Gulf Coast refineries, reflecting strong operational performance and its ability to capture favorable margins. Chevron Corporation CVX reported downstream earnings of $4.93 billion, compared with $1.14 billion a year earlier, supported by higher refined product margins. The company's U.S. refineries achieved record crude throughput of 1.09 million barrels per day, with utilization approaching 98%. Chevron's reliable refining operations highlight its ability to benefit from favorable market conditions. Suncor's shares have gained 67.5% over the past year, outperforming ExxonMobil's 46.3% increase and Chevron's 39.7% rise. SU's stronger share-price performance reflects investor interest in its integrated operations, improved cash generation and shareholder returns. The gains also highlight growing confidence in the company's ability to sustain profitability across its upstream and downstream businesses. Suncor appears attractively valued compared with its integrated energy peers. The stock trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 9.59, below ExxonMobil’s 13.26 and Chevron’s 12.45. This suggests that investors can gain exposure to Suncor’s expected earnings at a lower price than those of its larger peers. The valuation discount, combined with solid refining operations and healthy cash generation, adds to the stock’s investment appeal. Over the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Suncor's EPS has increased 18.54% for 2026 and 11.31% for 2027. The current estimates stand at $8.76 per share for 2026 and $7.28 for 2027. These upward revisions indicate improving analyst expectations for Suncor's earnings performance, supported by its integrated business model and favorable operating conditions. Suncor's strong refining performance, growing cash flow and integrated operations support its outlook. The stock’s attractive valuation relative to peers and upward earnings estimate revisions further strengthen its investment appeal, despite refining margin volatility.
